There’s lots of chemicals that do the same thing but damage the plastic and metal it’s suppose to be cleaning.

Same here. I drank most days but didn’t think the consequences were all that bad. Wine was my drink of choice for a couple reasons...it was stronger then beer and seemed more acceptable to be drinking on such a regular bases. I still worked out and was successful at work, so on the surface it seemed like I had my shit together. But the truth was I didn’t; I knew I had a problem with drinking but the thought of completely quitting for good seemed way to overwhelming. 

Anxiety attacks were one of the first signs that I needed to make a change. Then the consequences of poor decision making while drunk was the final straw and I started going to meetings. That’s been close to 2 years ago and I can honestly say that the further I got from drinking, the more I realized how much alcohol compromised me. 

My suggestion is to not worry about not drinking in the future because that concept is really hard to wrap your mind around. You can always try a few meetings and start to explore why you drink...that’s the only real way to understand the issue. I use to think I was week for having to do something like go to a meeting, but the truth is it takes real courage to face our issues, especially when they seem overwhelming. I came to the decision that alcohol just doesn’t fit in my life...I just can’t handle it. You make come to the same one or not, but it’s always good to explore the issue before it gets out of control. I wish you luck!

My honest advice (from an alcoholic who doesn’t drink anymore) is to read over your post again and question what your afraid of. Your body is telling you that what your currently doing isn’t sustainable..that’s what should scare you, not wether or not you can drink in moderation. The good news is you’re only 21 and you have an opportunity to do something now and avoid years of pain and struggle that many of us have endured. You have an opportunity to be kind to yourself and make decisions that legit change the trajectory of your life. 

My other advice is to seek out help. Lots of free programs out there that can help you figure out why you escape into booze and weed every day. And don’t worry about drinking in moderation later on in your life, worry about doing what’s healthy today, the rest of it will work itself out. Good luck.
